fullName.value: Vesicle transport through interaction with t-SNAREs homolog 1B

texts.value: SNAREs (soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor-attachment protein receptors) are essential proteins for intracellular membrane fusion. SNAREs localized on opposing membranes assemble to form a trans-SNARE complex, an extended, parallel four-helix bundle whose assembly releases energy that drives membrane fusion. The core SNARE complex typically consists of four alpha-helical domains, three from target membrane SNAREs (t-SNAREs) and one from a vesicle SNARE (v-SNARE) (PubMed:21388490, PubMed:23217709). On late endosomes, regulates trafficking from late endosomes to the lysosome (Probable)

Forms a SNARE complex with STX7, STX8 and VAMP8 which functions in the homotypic fusion of late endosomes (By similarity). Forms a SNARE complex composed of STX7, STX8, VAMP7 and VIT1B that is required for heterotypic fusion of late endosomes with lysosomes (By similarity). Interacts with STX11; the interaction is direct and positively regulates the SNAP receptor activity of VTI1B on late endosomes (PubMed:21388490). May interact with STX17 (PubMed:23217709). Interacts with CLINT1 (PubMed:18033301)
